title: Slow, Normal, Fast: One Playback, Three Speeds | vitalii.no
description:
Every sentence and grammar explanation in a language-learning app played back at one fixed tempo. Slower learners never got a chance to catch a fast phrase, and advanced learners sat through needless repeats at beginner speed.

runner/runner.py (Python) now walks a LADDER tempo tuple of 0.75x, 1.0x and 1.2x through a new ladder_seconds() helper, replacing the old flat repeat-count formula inside section_seconds() and word_seconds(). Word-level drills get their own slower tempo with a tighter 300ms gap between repeats, capped at ten words per batch, while full sentences use a 650ms gap. Grammar explanations get a dedicated time budget — up from a flat 350 seconds to 600 — and the grammar prompt itself was rewritten to drop dense grammar jargon in favor of plain-word explanations. The same formula was ported to the dashboard's JavaScript so the estimated video length shown on screen matches what actually renders, and a new 'Сходинка темпу' dropdown lets a learner choose all tempos, grammar only, or off.

A learner can now hear a sentence slow, normal and fast in one pass instead of one fixed speed, with the estimated video length shown upfront finally matching the real render time — three speeds where there used to be one.
